groups.label: OTP IP
groups.description: One-time programming can store charge or alter a dielectric; these are different cell mechanisms.

groups.label: MTP IP
groups.description: Compare how electrons enter the floating node and how electron removal or hole injection reverses the state.

groups.label: MRAM IP
groups.description: Read embedded macros through their junctions, access transistors and electrical paths.

groups.label: ReRAM IP
groups.description: Follow oxygen-related defects or metallic paths through SET, RESET and sensing.

units.title: NeoBit: Floating-Gate OTP Cell
units.summary: Follow the series select transistor and p-type floating-gate storage transistor as electron injection changes read current. Then distinguish normal OTP operation from the physical possibility of ultraviolet erasure.
units.reverse: No electrical erase in normal OTP operation
units.lesson: A floating-gate OTP stores its state in charge. The selector controls access, while programming moves the storage transistor to another sensed state. An interface without electrical erase is a different OTP design path from an irreversible dielectric change.

units.title: NeoFuse: Gate-Dielectric Antifuse OTP Cell
units.summary: Start at the n-type cell's gate dielectric and follow high-field defect creation, changes in effective tunneling distance and the gate current used for sensing.
units.reverse: No restoration of the pristine dielectric in normal use
units.lesson: The storage event changes dielectric conduction. An ideal short does not explain the ultrathin-dielectric physics. Selection and regulation transistors support array operation; defects and tunneling in the storage region create the programmed read-current difference.

units.title: NeoEE: FN/FN Single-Poly MTP
units.summary: Follow the control-coupling region, floating node and tunneling region as FN transport stores and removes electrons. A read transistor then senses the stored state.
units.program: FN transfers electrons into the floating node
units.reverse: FN transfers electrons out of the floating node
units.lesson: Both update directions use tunneling, but field direction, selection and biased regions must still be distinguished. Single poly describes layer count; the division of work among coupling, tunneling and read devices explains this IP's update path.

units.title: NeoMTP: CHI/FN Single-Poly MTP
units.summary: Compare hot-carrier programming of the p-type floating-gate cell with FN electron transfer toward a dedicated erase gate. Both operations act on the same storage node.
units.reverse: FN electron transfer toward the erase gate
units.lesson: CHI/FN is the operation-pair shorthand used here. eMemory describes programming as channel-hot-hole-induced hot-electron injection and labels it CHEI. The erase gate provides a separate electron exit, distinguishing this cell from NeoBit's normal OTP interface and NeoEE's FN/FN mechanism.

units.title: YMC MTP: CHI/BBHH Operation Model
units.summary: Use the same equivalent 1T1C floating node to follow CHI electron programming and BBHH hole injection, then read the state through nMOS threshold voltage and channel current.
units.program: CHI injects electrons into the floating node
units.reverse: BBHH injects holes to neutralize stored charge
units.lesson: This is the CHI/BBHH mechanism model selected for this course. Public YMC material supports its logic-process MTP IP positioning; independent primary research supports the BBHH physics. The figure is not identified as a complete cross-section of a current ymtp version. FN, drain-avalanche hot-hole injection and band-to-band hot-hole injection are distinct paths, even when related patents share an assignee.

units.title: Numem: Embedded STT-MRAM IP Cell
units.summary: Connect foundry-standard STT-MRAM cells to embedded IP by identifying the magnetic junction, access transistor, bit line, source line and sensing path.
units.reverse: Opposite write current overwrites the state
units.lesson: Numem can use foundry-standard STT cells while integrating its layout, circuits and memory architecture. Understand the two junction states and access/sense paths before considering macro behavior; a control-architecture improvement is not a new storage mechanism.

units.title: GLOBALFOUNDRIES: 22FDX Embedded MRAM Cell
units.summary: Use a publicly reported 22FDX research cell to examine 1T1MTJ, free and reference layers, and bidirectional switching under the source's current convention.
units.program: Switch under the named study's polarity convention
units.reverse: Reverse overwrite; no prior erase cycle
units.readout: Sense P/AP resistance with a small stimulus
units.lesson: A foundry embedded macro joins the magnetic junction to logic processing, the access transistor and reliability conditions. This figure retains the named study's materials and polarity convention for step-by-step reading; those details do not automatically describe every current 22FDX memory version.

units.title: Weebit Nano: Silicon-Oxide ReRAM IP Cell
units.summary: Follow oxygen exchange, a defect-related conduction path and access-transistor current compliance in a public silicon-oxide research structure to understand embedded ReRAM SET, RESET and read.
units.program: SET establishes a low-resistance defect path
units.reverse: RESET changes oxygen and defect distributions
units.readout: Sense resistance with a small stimulus
units.lesson: In this named research example, the storage medium, oxygen-exchange electrode and access transistor jointly shape switching. Current compliance and read stimulus are part of cell operation. Materials and recipes remain scoped to the cited implementation.

units.title: Crossbar: Metallic-Path Embedded ReRAM Cell
units.summary: Read Crossbar's public patent and historical embedded-macro materials through metallic-path extension, retraction and low-stimulus sensing.
units.reverse: RESET retracts or disconnects the path
units.lesson: This figure follows the named patent's metal/amorphous-silicon model. Do not substitute another ECM cell's nucleation direction or an ideal continuous silver bridge. Evidence for the embedded macro and for the historical cell embodiment is identified separately.
